title: Derivation of partition relationships to calculate Cd, Cu, Ni, Pb and Zn solubility and activity in soil solutions
water_body: Dutch soils: soil extracts/solutions, database of 1466 complete records
measure: Kd
notes: Sign convention: paper reports regression coefficient on pH directly (log10 units); positive Kd coefficient = more sorption at higher pH, same as this schema. Model (refit in the form of Sauvé et al. 2000): log Kd = 0.43*pH + 0.7*log(OM%) + (-0.18); R2 = 0.64, se(Y) = 0.59. Kd = Q (mg/kg) / C (ug/L), Freundlich n fixed at 1. Soils, not fresh waters. Reactive metal Q = 0.43 M HNO3 extraction; dissolved C in 1:2 soil:solution extracts made with mixed electrolytes (0.002, 0.01 or 0.1 M CaCl2 or Ca(NO3)2, 0.03 M NaNO3) plus some pore waters, so ionic strength and Ca vary between sub-datasets. Report gives dataset pH as 'min 1.8, max 7.9' (as transcribed; verify). n = 1466 complete records in database; n used per regression not confirmed. Multiple regression, so the pH coefficient is a partial slope conditional on the other terms. Values transcribed via a text-extraction tool and cross-checked by a second read.
